messages:
caroline: RFC follow-up — we keep hitting fuzzy ownership between Hosted / Dedicated / Private. proposing a very small ownership matrix so teams don't keep arguing about who rotates certs, who owns rollouts, and where billing gets enforced. thoughts?
ajay: +1. big thing for me: Dedicated (reserved capacity) sits in the middle — customers expect us to operate infra but also want isolation. we should avoid duplicating rollout codepaths.
ben: can we make this tangible by adding explicit owner fields to the adapter manifest? example:
```
adapter_manifest:
  name: model-adapter
  owners:
    auth: control-plane
    rollout: runtime-ops
    billing_meter: metering-proxy
    telemetry: telemetry-agent
    cert_rotation: control-plane
    sla_contact: runtime-oncall
  fallback_policy: local-first
```
that would let infra/runtime read an authoritative source.
denise: big +1 to manifest owners. question: billing_meter in Private — we can't push raw usage to our billing service. we need a minimal metering-proxy interface that emits signed aggregates. otherwise enterprise licensing breaks.
lucas: also need explicit fallback semantics. Hosted: we can route to a cheaper hosted model. Dedicated: might have partner fallback (same datacenter). Private: no external fallback unless customer opts in. manifest flag like `fallback_policy: [local, dedicated, hosted]` is helpful.
caroline: yes — separate out capability from policy. capability = what the environment is allowed to do (eg: outbound network allowed?), policy = what we will actually do. keep both in the manifest.
ajay: ops implication: oncall handovers are messy. for Dedicated we should keep runtime-oncall inside Redwood for infra-level incidents, and customer SRE for app-level incidents. put that into runbook templates.
ben: runbook template sketch in thread:
```
-- runbook: dedicated-upgrade
pre-req:
  - customer signed upgrade window
  - snapshot KV and model cache
responsibility:
  runtime_upgrades: redwood-runtime-oncall
  model_rollout: customer-sre OR redwood-runtime (contract)
  post-checks: telemetry-agent -> ownership: telemetry
```
we can later translate into a playbook generator.
denise: security corner: KMS ownership must be explicit. Private often uses customer KMS; Dedicated may use customer KMS or Redwood-managed. adapter manifest needs kms.owner and kms.mode.
lucas: latency SLO mapping: who owns SLO interpretation? example: 99th token latency for hosted is our obligation. for Dedicated it's a blended expectation: we guarantee pod stability, customer owns worst-case network tail. we need to document where SLO boundaries stop.
caroline: action items I propose: 1) ajay to draft ownership matrix doc, 2) ben to open manifest PR with owner fields + example schemas, 3) denise to propose metering-proxy interface + threat model, 4) lucas to write SLO boundary note. aim: RFC follow-up in two weeks.
ajay: I can take point on the matrix. will include quick tables: auth, rollout, billing, telemetry, kms, certs, oncall, fallback. will tag runtime, control-plane, customer-sre where applicable.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary adapter-manifest-v2 -> staging at 2026-03-21T13:00:00Z :rocket:
caroline: perfect. let's keep the manifest minimal for v1 and don't bake policy engines yet — just clear owners and capability flags. we can iterate. :thumbsup:
ben: minor note: add `audit_sink` owner for Private deployments so compliance teams know where logs go.
denise: +1. also include a small checklist for handing off Private installs: certs, KMS access, runbook link, metering proxy endpoint, telemetry endpoint, emergency rollback token.
lucas: will add a small fallback-state diagram to the SLO doc so product teams understand failure modes.
caroline: ok closing thread for now — ajay please ping #architecture when draft ready. thanks everyone. :doughnut:
